results.title: NASA's Voyager 1 phones home from record one light-day away, 49 years after launch
results.content: The Voyager 1 probe launched by NASA nearly a half century ago has reached a distance from Earth of one light day (more than 26 billion kilometres), the farthest any human artifact has ever ventured from our planet. The space agency received a signal from the spacecraft Thursday, exactly 24 hours after it was sent.

results.title: French media regulator says it will monitor top YouTubers for bias in election coverage
results.content: Rules designed to safeguard media pluralism during elections campaigns will apply to France's most influential YouTubers in the run-up to next year's presidential contest, media regulator Arcom warned on Thursday, reflecting the growing influence of content creators whose audiences often outstrip those of traditional media companies.

results.title: What impact will the Shenzhen summit have on the US-China trade war?
results.content: Despite warm words between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping at three-way talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen Thursday, the simmering trade war between Washington and Beijing still looks to be no closer to resolution.

results.title: Bangladesh: Hasina supporters vandalise ruling party office
results.content: Hundreds of supporters of ousted Bangladesh premier Sheikh Hasina staged street protests on Thursday, as a wave of arson attacks escalated tensions ahead of her planned return from exile next month.

results.title: US has 'unbalanced approach' on DR Congo deal, Rwanda's foreign minister says
results.content: In an interview with FRANCE 24, Rwandan Foreign Minister Olivier Nduhungirehe said the Trump administration had "an unbalanced approach" in implementing the DR Congo peace deal it brokered. He also said that the recent row over the Organisation Internationale de la Francophonie's top job was "manufactured in Paris and Kinshasa". Finally, he defended a deal for Rwanda to host failed asylum seekers from five European countries.

results.title: 🔴Anthropic soars more than 30% to $2 trillion valuation on first day of trading
How much do businesses want to pay for AI?
results.content: Four years after ChatGPT went mainstream, generative AI is transforming how we live and work. It's also been a major driver of economic growth, with massive amounts of money poured into expanding global computing capacity. But now, there are signs of a slowdown in AI spending as companies take a reality check: are they getting sufficient returns on their investments and how much artificial intelligence do they actually need?

results.title: Inside France's mental health crisis: Are the French all right?
results.content: This week, we try to get inside the heads of French people, with a deep dive into mental health in France. For a nation that loves analysing its problems, its mental health figures make for sobering reading: nearly one in five French people are affected by a mental health issue.

results.title: ICJ ruling on Myanmar genocide: ‘Historic victory for Rohingya, landmark for international justice’
results.content: Erin Ogunkeye welcomes Reed Brody, Member of the International Commission of Jurists, Human Rights Lawyer and veteran war crimes prosecutor. The International Court of Justice's ruling on Myanmar marks, according to Brody, "a historic victory for the Rohingya, but also a landmark for international justice." He explains how the court assessed evidence of genocidal intent, rejecting Myanmar's justification of its military operations as counterterrorism. He argues that "the existence of an armed conflict or a security objective doesn't exclude genocidal intent," a finding he believes will have "far-reaching implications in future genocide cases," including South Africa's case against Israel over Gaza. Brody also discusses the Gambia's role in bringing the case and growing challenges to international accountability, warning that "we're in a very dangerous moment."

results.title: Xi demonstrating China's 'global status', occupying 'central position' in relation to Trump & Putin
results.content: Sharon Gaffney is pleased to welcome Rex Li, professor of international relations at King's College London. For Professor Li, the meeting between Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin in China is less about "reaching concrete agreements and a common position." Rather, he argues, it is about demonstrating Xi's ability to bring the American and Russian leaders together to discuss major geopolitical issues. Li believes that Xi Jinping has the most to gain from the meeting, as it allows him to demonstrate China's global status and its role as a diplomatic convener. Putin may also benefit from the opportunity to meet the two leaders despite Russia's international isolation following its invasion of Ukraine.

results.title: Gender pay gap: French women work "for free” from today
results.content: Women in Europe are still paid less than men, with the gap falling from 15.1% in 2016 to 11.1% in 2024, according to Eurostat. In France, women symbolically start working for free from 10:51 am on Thursday, 19 November, and at the current pace equality would not be reached until 2062. Experts warn that AI could make things worse by eliminating administrative and legal jobs where many women work, while childbirth and short paternity leave continue to slow women’s careers.

results.title: 'GTA VI': A masterpiece? Fans react to gaming's biggest release
results.content: Critics are calling the new "Grand Theft Auto VI" a masterpiece. In this edition of arts24, we hear what fans make of one of the biggest video game releases in history. We also look at U2's new album and tour marking 50 years of the band, discover the French comic book that Pope Leo is reading and meet the women redefining Mexico's Mariachi tradition.

results.title: The chocolate countdown: The art of the advent calendar
results.content: The holiday season is almost upon us and with it come advent calendars. The annual physical countdown originated in 19th-century Germany as a Christian tradition to count down the days until Christmas. Eugénie Pont from the magazine Fou de Pâtisserie tells us more about what we can expect from the biggest chocolate makers in France.

results.title: Trump, Xi, Putin summit: What was it all about?
results.content: Donald Trump has left China after a historic first meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the APEC summit. Ukraine was discussed without Kyiv or European leaders in the room, which raised eyebrows, though Trump defended dialogue with rivals and Putin said the talks created conditions for future agreements. Xi warned major powers against conflict, and topics included reducing nuclear risks, reforming the UN and increasing energy flows.

results.title: Behind the UK's use of AI in asylum applications
results.content: The UK is increasingly turning to artificial intelligence to manage its immigration system, from analysing migrants’ phones to processing asylum applications. But what happens when AI gets involved in deciding how an asylum seeker's story is understood? Stella Elgersma, journalist at InfoMigrants, explains how the UK Home Office is testing AI tools to process asylum applications, including a system that generates summaries of asylum interviews. With errors, limited human oversight and concerns over transparency, could AI put asylum seekers’ lives at risk?

results.title: Haiti: Salvador’s Bukele publishes video of attack on gang leader’s house
results.content: Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele said Wednesday that his troops demolished the lavish home of a prominent gang leader in Haiti known as Jeff Gwo Lwa. "My gift to the Haitian people on the anniversary of the Battle of Vertières," Bukele wrote on X - referencing a 1803 battle critical in helping secure Haiti's independence from France.

results.title: Beaujolais Nouveau: A French tradition uncorked
results.content: Every year on the third Thursday of November, France raises a glass to one of its most joyful traditions: Le Beaujolais Nouveau! That means that this Thursday, millions of bottles of the 2026 young red wine will be uncorked around the world, from Lyon to New York. Olivier Badoureaux, wine expert and director of the French trade organisation Inter Beaujolais, tells us what we should expect from this year's vintage.

results.title: France: Retirees march against 2027 budget cuts
results.content: More than a thousand people marched in Paris on Thursday, called by a union alliance joined by student and high-school groups, to protest social and tax measures targeting retirees in the 2027 budgets. The government wants retirees to contribute about €5.4 billion, by freezing the indexation of pensions above €1,260 and reforming their 10% income tax allowance. Union leaders say the money should not come from retirees’ pockets, as FRANCE 24's Luke Shrago explains.

results.title: 🔴 AI firm Anthropic begins trading on Nasdaq, aiming to raise $81 billion in biggest IPO on record
Anthropic blows past $2 trillion in Nasdaq debut, beating SpaceX's June listing
results.content: Anthropic hit $2 trillion in market value as its shares soared in their Nasdaq debut on Thursday, with investors rushing to own a stake in the maker of the Claude chatbot, the world's first publicly traded frontier AI company. Shares began trading at $111.5, 34% higher than the IPO price of $83.

results.title: Chef Rachel Khoo: 'You don't need fancy kitchen gadgets to cook delicious food'
results.content: One of the world's best-known chefs has spoken to FRANCE 24 about her new book that proves you certainly don't need fancy kitchen gadgets to cook delicious meals. The book "The Smallest Restaurant in Paris" tells her own story of starting out in a tiny Parisian flat cooking food just for two people at a time. That then led to a BBC series and a decade of writing and filming cooking stories. Rachel Khoo is now a judge on "The Great Australian Bake Off". She spoke to us in Perspective.

results.title: ICJ rules Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya
results.content: In August 2017, after attacks by a Rohingya militia, Myanmar’s army launched a “clearance campaign” in Rakhine state, with survivors describing mass killings, rapes and burned villages as hundreds of thousands fled to Bangladesh. The Gambia took Myanmar to the ICJ in 2019, and after a seven-year legal fight the court has ruled that Myanmar committed acts of genocide. Meanwhile some 1.2 million Rohingya remain in crowded camps, unable to return home.

results.title: China summit ends with little new, Europe backs Ukraine in Berlin
results.content: The leaders of China, the United States and Russia met in Shenzhen for a historic first, but the summit brought little new: non-binding statements on peace and no plan to meet regularly. In Berlin, Europeans gathered to show their support for Ukraine, a pointed answer to a summit where Europe had no seat, as FRANCE 24's Kethevane Gorjestani explains.

results.title: In South Korea, women forced into prostitution on US military bases seek justice
results.content: Tens of thousands of women were forced to work in South Korean state-sanctioned brothels used by American soldiers based in the country after the Korean War. They were raped, physically abused and forcibly confined. Now, after decades of silence, some of these women are speaking out.
